title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 36
paragraphs: During this same time there appeared on Mysian Olympus a boar of monstrous size. Coming down from that mountain, it ravaged the fields of the Mysians, and though the Mysians went out against it often, they could do it no harm but rather suffered harm from it themselves. At length messengers came from the Mysians to Croesus and said: “O king, a boar of monstrous size has appeared in our land and is laying waste our fields. Though we eagerly wish to take it, we are unable. We therefore ask you to send with us your son along with a chosen band of young men and dogs, so that we may drive this creature out of our land.” So they made their request, and Croesus, calling to mind the words of the dream, spoke to them as follows: “As for my son, make no further mention of him in this matter, for I will not send him with you. He is newly married and is occupied now with the business of his marriage. But I will send with you chosen Lydian men and the whole of my pack of hunting dogs, and I will order those who go to be as zealous as possible in helping you drive the wild beast out of your land.”
